title: Kkaennip Jangajji Pickled Perilla Leaves
shortDescription: Perilla leaves are layered with a cooled soy-vinegar brine for a crisp, savory refrigerator pickle that is never presented as shelf-stable.
culturalContext: Kkaennip jangajji is a preserved perilla-leaf banchan with household variations in brine, aromatics, sweetness, and resting time. This draft uses a vinegar-forward refrigerator method rather than a canning process.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: stems trimmed; washed under running water and dried

instructions.heading: Wash and dry
instructions.action: Rinse leaves individually under cool running water, drain, and dry thoroughly; do not use soap or produce wash.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are clean, intact, and dry.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard slimy or damaged leaves and use clean hands and tools.

instructions.heading: Make brine
instructions.action: Combine soy sauce, 5% acidity rice vinegar, water, sugar, garlic, and optional gochugaru; bring to a brief boil while stirring.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sugar dissolves and brine bubbles throughout.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only commercially labeled 5% acidity vinegar; prevent steam and splash burns.

instructions.heading: Cool completely
instructions.action: Transfer brine to a clean heat-safe bowl and cool completely before it touches the leaves.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not pour hot brine into an unsuitable container or directly onto delicate leaves.

instructions.heading: Layer cleanly
instructions.action: Layer leaves in a clean container, spooning cooled brine between every few leaves.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are evenly wetted and mostly submerged.
instructions.safetyNote: Minimize time out of refrigeration and never reuse a container that is not clean.

instructions.heading: Refrigerate
instructions.action: Cover and refrigerate at least 12 hours, pressing leaves below the brine with a clean utensil after the first hour.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves darken slightly and absorb brine.
instructions.safetyNote: This is a refrigerator pickle only, not a shelf-stable or fermentation process.

instructions.heading: Serve cold
instructions.action: Remove portions with clean utensils and return the container promptly to refrigeration.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves smell fresh and savory with no gas, slime, or mold.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard the entire batch if mold, gas, slime, or an off odor appears.

grillSetup: No grill required; use a clean preparation area separate from raw meat and seafood.
targetInternalTemperature: Keep continuously refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C.
visualDonenessCues: Brine remains clear of mold or gas
No slime or off odor is present
foodSafetyNotes: Refrigerator pickle only; not shelf-stable, canned, or validated for room-temperature storage.
Use commercial vinegar labeled 5% acidity and do not reduce the vinegar proportion without a qualified process review.
Keep at or below 40°F / 4°C and use a clean utensil for every serving.
Discard the batch if it was held above 40°F / 4°C for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after label verification.
Do not substitute homemade or unlabeled vinegar.
ingredientSourcing: Choose unwilted perilla leaves without slime.
Confirm the vinegar label states 5% acidity.
makeAhead: Prepare 12 to 24 hours ahead and keep continuously refrigerated.
storage: Keep covered at or below 40°F / 4°C and use within 5 days; this conservative limit requires test-kitchen review.
reheating: Do not reheat; serve cold with a clean utensil.
leftovers: Return promptly to refrigeration; discard portions left out beyond time limits or contaminated by used utensils.
servingSuggestions: Serve one folded leaf with rice and grilled meat.
Use clean kitchen shears to cut leaves for diners who need smaller bites.

faq.question: Can I store this in the pantry?
faq.answer: No. This draft is a refrigerator pickle only and is not a validated canning process.

faq.question: Can I use any vinegar?
faq.answer: Use only commercially labeled 5% acidity vinegar unless a qualified process authority approves another formula.
